verdictReason: Phase 5 canonical-authority, link-firewall, and buffer-then-validate invariants re-verified unchanged from a clean checkout before any change. Added observable routeMode across all response branches (JSON and streaming), structured source metadata wired into streaming and the visitor UI (previously absent from the streaming path entirely), two new multi-turn false-premise corrections (founder pronoun follow-up, fabricated-pricing carryover), and a golden corpus expansion from 113 to 150. One real accessibility defect (Tab focus-trap escape) was found via live interactive browser testing and fixed. One self-inflicted regression (a price-rejection answer colliding with the verifier's own strict price detector) was caught by the existing false-positive suite and fixed on the answer side, not by weakening the verifier. Deployed to production and live-verified with 15/15 HTTP 200 across canonical, conversational, comparison, GEMS-synthesis, page-context, unknown-fact, injection, fabricated-pricing, fabricated-founder, and external-link-attack categories. Live PROVIDER_ACCEPTED execution was not observed this phase (see knownLimitations) and is reported as such rather than inferred from passing mocks.

selfCaughtRegression.description: First version of the fabricated-pricing rejection echoed the exact figure ('$49') back to the visitor as part of explaining why it was false; verify.ts's checkPrice() has no negation awareness by design (unlike checkVersions/checkAvailability/checkBenchmarks/checkCancellation/checkFounder, which all check isNegated() first), so the false-positive sweep in kayla-verify.test.ts correctly flagged Kayla's own new canonical answer as a violation.
selfCaughtRegression.caughtBy: test/kayla-verify.test.ts (pre-existing Phase 5 false-positive sweep, not new this phase)
selfCaughtRegression.resolution: Changed the answer text to not echo the literal figure, per the instruction not to weaken already-certified verifier strictness to make a new feature's test pass. verify.ts was not modified.

accessibilityFindings.foundVia: live interactive browser testing (Browser tool), not code inspection
accessibilityFindings.description: Tab focus trap's focusable-element query filtered on el.hidden (DOM property), but the starters row and the stop button are hidden via style.display, which that property does not reflect. The trap computed 'last focusable element' as an invisible control (the stop button, present after any message is sent), so a real Tab press from the last visible control never matched the boundary check and focus escaped the open, aria-modal dialog into the rest of the page — confirmed by direct DOM inspection (document.activeElement landed on the page's own skip-link while the dialog remained visibly open).
accessibilityFindings.fix: Added `&& el.offsetParent !== null` to the focusable-element filter in KaylaCopilot.ts.
accessibilityFindings.verifiedLive: 6 Tab presses from the composer now correctly cycle within the panel (close -> input -> send -> wrap); a dispatched Shift+Tab from the first control correctly wraps to the last.
accessibilityFindings.automatedRegressionTest: test/kayla-ui-contract.test.ts asserts the fix is present in source; no jsdom environment is configured in this project, so a full DOM-level assertion was not possible and is not claimed.

providerLaneProof.likelyExplanation: Shared 40-request/day AI allowance (KAYLA_AI_DAILY_REQUEST_LIMIT) most likely already consumed by Phase 5's own same-day live testing (their receipt records 9 AI-success + 6 timeout samples earlier the same UTC day) plus this phase's own attempts. Fast (169ms-742ms) non-timeout-shaped failures across 5 distinct query types support an allowance/availability denial rather than a provider timeout (configured at 9000ms). Not independently confirmed via a debug counter, since adding one was out of scope.
providerLaneProof.recommendedFollowUp: Re-run a small live provider-lane sample early in a fresh UTC day, or after confirming no other same-day testing has consumed the allowance.

knownLimitations: Live PROVIDER_ACCEPTED and PROVIDER_REPLACED were not observed in production this phase; only PROVIDER_FAILURE_LOCAL_FALLBACK was, and it worked correctly every time it was observed.
verifyAgainstCanon() remains pattern-based and cannot catch a subtly wrong relationship between two individually-true facts (unchanged from Phase 5).
The focus-trap fix has no jsdom-level automated test; verified live and guarded by a source-presence regression test only.
Retrieval nuance, not a defect: 'What is that coding thing?' resolves to Sapphire rather than CodeForge; both are defensible given Sapphire's own role text.

A meta-question about the public-vs-research status taxonomy itself ('What's the difference between a public project and a research project here?') resolves to a specific project via retrieval rather than explaining the taxonomy; building a dedicated answer for this was out of scope.
